title: Later Jin
capsule: The Later Jin (後晉, 936–947) was the third of the Five Dynasties that successively ruled northern China after the fall of the Tang, founded when the Shatuo general Shi Jingtang allied with the Khitan Liao empire to overthrow the Later Tang — ceding the strategically vital Sixteen Prefectures of Yan and Yun to the Liao as the price of military support. Shi Jingtang (Emperor Gaozu, r. 936–942) maintained a submissive posture toward the Liao, but his nephew Shi Chonggui (Emperor Chu, r. 942–947) broke from that deference; the Liao invaded in 946, sacked Kaifeng in 947, and extinguished the dynasty. The concession of the Sixteen Prefectures, never recovered by any successor Chinese state, would deprive northern China of its defensive buffer for centuries.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political and dynastic history is well documented in the Old and New Histories of the Five Dynasties (Jiu Wudai Shi, Xin Wudai Shi); territorial extent over the North China Plain is clear, though frontier zones are approximated.
